summary: Defines an extension to the Dynamic Link Exchange Protocol that lets a radio modem use DLEP messages to ask its attached router to pause and later resume sending traffic. It is useful when the modem cannot keep up with what the router sends.

eli5.summary: When a bucket is full, you tell the person pouring to stop for a moment. This lets a radio modem say stop and go to its router.

questions: what is the dlep pause extension
how does dlep flow control work
what is a dlep queue index
subtitle: How a radio modem tells its router to stop sending traffic, and when it can start again.

tldr.problem: The base Dynamic Link Exchange Protocol (DLEP) has no data-plane flow control, so a modem has no way to tell its router to hold off when it cannot keep up.
tldr.mechanism: This extension adds three DLEP Data Items: Queue Parameters, Pause and Restart. A modem sends them in session and destination update messages to stop and resume traffic, either for everything or per DSCP-based queue.
tldr.outcome: A router that receives a Pause MUST stop sending the identified traffic, and one that receives a Restart SHOULD resume. It is a Proposed Standard.

facts.label: Reserved Queue Index in sub-data items

today: RFC 8651 is a Proposed Standard published in October 2019 and has not been obsoleted. It extends DLEP as defined in RFC 8175.

sections.title: Why DLEP Needs a Pause
sections.content:
The Dynamic Link Exchange Protocol (DLEP, RFC 8175) lets a modem and a router exchange link-related control information. DLEP allows extensions, and the base specification includes no data-plane flow-control capability. This document defines an extension called Control-Plane-Based Pause, in which the modem sends explicit DLEP messages to say when the router should hold off and when it should resume.

The RFC says this parallels the flow control in PPP over Ethernet (RFC 5578). It can optionally be aware of DSCPs (Differentiated Services Code Points), which is similar to Ethernet priority-based flow control. Other flow-control methods are possible with DLEP.

The mechanism applies only to traffic sent from the router to the modem on the single subnetwork joining them. It does not apply to DLEP control messages themselves.
sections.eli5: A modem is like a small doorway and the router is a crowd pushing through. This extension lets the doorway say "wait a moment" when it is jammed.

sections.title: Turning the Extension On
sections.content: Use of the extension SHOULD be configurable. An implementation that supports it MUST include the Control-Plane-Based Pause Extension Type Value in the Extensions Supported Data Item, which is sent and processed as described in RFC 8175. The Extension Type Value is 2.
sections.eli5: Both sides say "I know the stop and go signals" when they first meet, so they know they can use them.

sections.title: Queue Parameters
sections.content:
The modem uses the Queue Parameters Data Item (type 23) to describe the DSCPs it forwards, grouped into logical queues. It MUST be included in a Session Initialization Response Message that also lists this extension, and it MAY be updated later in Session Update Messages.

Each queue has a Queue Index numbered sequentially from zero. Index zero is a special case that covers DSCPs not otherwise assigned to a queue. A queue size in bytes is given for information only. An implementation that does not support DSCPs indicates one queue with zero DSCPs.

The item has a Num Queues field (at least one), a 4-bit Scale field and a list of Queue Parameter Sub-Data Items. The Scale values are 0 for bytes, 1 for kilobytes, 2 for megabytes and 3 for gigabytes. Each sub-data item (Sub-Data Item Type 1) holds a Queue Index, a 24-bit Queue Size, the number of DSCPs and that many 8-bit DS fields. The Queue Index value 255 is reserved and MUST NOT be used here. Parsing errors are handled like any other DLEP Data Item error: the receiver sends a Session Termination Message with status code 130 (Invalid Data).
sections.eli5: The modem first tells the router how many lines it has for different kinds of traffic, so later it can say which line to stop.

sections.title: The Pause and Restart Data Items
sections.content:
The Pause Data Item (type 24) tells the router to suppress traffic. The motivating case is a modem queue that grows past a threshold. The Restart Data Item (type 25) tells the router that it may resume, for example when the queue drops below a threshold.

Both items have the same format: a Type, a Length and one or more 8-bit Queue Index values. A Queue Index refers to a queue defined by Queue Parameters. The special value 255 means all traffic. Length equals the number of Queue Index fields carried.
sections.eli5: Pause is a red light and Restart is a green light, and each light can be for one lane or for every lane.

sections.title: How Pause and Restart Behave
sections.content:
A modem can pause traffic for the whole device or for one destination. To pause everything, it MUST send the Pause Data Item in a Session Update Message. To pause a single destination, it MUST send it in a Destination Update Message. A modem SHOULD put multiple queue indexes in the same message when possible. Restart follows the same rules.

A router that receives a Pause MUST cease sending the identified traffic to the modem, which may make the router's own queues exceed their thresholds. If the Queue Index is neither 255 nor one set up by a Session Initialization or Session Update Message, the router MUST terminate the session with an "Invalid Data" status. A router that receives Restart SHOULD resume sending.
sections.eli5: The modem can say stop to everybody or only to one friend. The router has to obey a stop, and should start again when told to.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The extension adds no vulnerabilities that differ in kind from those in RFC 8175, and the same security approach applies. Implementations MUST support configuring and using TLS as described in that RFC, to protect setups where injection attacks are possible because the modem-router link is not otherwise protected.

A compromised or impersonating modem could use this extension to suppress transmission by the router or by a switch between the modem and router. The RFC notes that similar attacks are generally possible with base DLEP, such as a session reset or simply dropping traffic, and that TLS protects against impersonation.
sections.eli5: If a fake modem shouts stop, the router might stop. Locking the connection with TLS makes sure only the real modem can give the order.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA assigned Extension Type Value 2 (Control-Plane-Based Pause) and Data Item Type Values 23 (Queue Parameters), 24 (Pause) and 25 (Restart), all under the Specification Required policy. It also created a new registry, Queue Parameter Sub-Data Item Type Values, with 0 reserved, 1 for Queue Parameter, 2 to 65407 as Specification Required, 65408 to 65534 for Private Use and 65535 reserved.
sections.eli5: The numbers for the new stop and go signals were written in an official list so nobody else uses them for something different.

items.desc: Data Item telling the router to stop sending identified traffic.
